name: SObjectizer
listed_description: An implementation of Actor, Publish-Subscribe, and CSP models in one rather small C++ framework.
reason: No numeric comparison against a named baseline in any reachable source. The README states that comparing SObjectizer with TBB, taskflow or HPX is useless (concurrent computing, not parallel computing) and gives no benchmark figures. The repo's dev/test/so_5/bench programs (skynet1m, ping_pong, agent_ring, thread_pool_disp and others) time SObjectizer alone with no other framework in them. The SourceForge FAQ gives only an absolute figure (1.5-2 to 8-10 million messages per second on a four-core Core i7) with no baseline. The author's 2016 article 'Performance Comparison SO-5.5.15.2 vs CAF-0.14.4' (linked from the wiki articles-en page and the FAQ) is hosted on eao197.blogspot.com, which the egress proxy blocks, so its numbers could not be read; it is a first-party comparison against CAF 0.14.4 and a possible lead for a later pass from an environment that can reach it. Marco Arena's 'SObjectizer Tales' performance series (marcoarena.wordpress.com, dev.to, isocpp.org) was also unreachable.

name: STAPL
listed_description: A C++ parallel programming framework designed to work on both shared and distributed memory parallel computers.
reason: No numeric comparison against a named baseline in any reachable source. The GitLab repo README (BSD-2-Clause) describes a benchmarks directory of STAPL ports of benchmarks collected from various sources and OSU message-passing microbenchmarks but reports no numbers and no comparison with TBB, OpenMP, MPI or the STL. WebSearch snippets show only the 2003 paper's claim that STL code translated to STAPL runs within 5 percent of hand-written STAPL (STAPL against itself) and scalability studies of STAPL alone. The project site (parasol-lab.gitlab.io), the Illinois publication pages and the SYSTOR 2010 slides did not resolve (egress blocked), so any comparison inside the papers could not be checked.

name: STLport
reason: Directional claims only, no numbers on any page that could be opened. The SourceForge project page (license 'Other', last update 2019-04-04) says 'Maximum efficiency' and carries one 2010 user review saying it is faster than the STL shipped with MSVC, with no measurement. The project site www.stlport.org did not resolve. WebSearch snippets point to a 2010 LibreOffice developer-list post (libstdc++ against STLport 4.5, native STL usually faster except for large maps and some std::string cases) and a forum anecdote of a 25 percent whole-application gain on HP-UX; neither page could be opened, and the first is mixed rather than a win.

name: templog
listed_description: A very small and lightweight C++ library which you can use to add logging to your C++ applications.
reason: Project site www.templog.org did not resolve (getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND) and two WebSearch queries found no mirror, repository, package page or benchmark mentioning templog. No numeric comparison with std::cerr or any logging library could be found.

name: termbox
listed_description: A C library for writing text-based user interfaces.
reason: README (MIT) makes no performance claim and has no benchmark; its only ncurses mention is a v1.1.1 changelog line about an ncurses 6.1 compatibility fix. The README states the library is no longer maintained. A WebSearch for termbox against ncurses benchmarks found none (termbox2 ports mention only more efficient escape-sequence parsing, not measured).

name: TermOx
reason: README (MIT, C++20 rewrite 'TermOx II', 877 stars) lists layout, events, styling and widgets only; no benchmark directory (docs, examples, include, src, tests) and no performance claim or comparison with ncurses, termbox or any other TUI library.

name: tgc
listed_description: A tiny garbage collector for C written in ~500 LOC.
reason: Directional claim only. The README FAQ 'Is tgc fast?' says performance is 'decent' and 'competative with many existing memory management systems' but 'definitely can't claim to be the fastest garbage collector on the market', names no system and gives no numbers. The repo holds only tgc.c, tgc.h, a Makefile and examples/ (no benchmark), and a WebSearch for tgc against Boehm GC or malloc timings found none.
